title: Add the WEIGHTED parent roll-up to the Work Progress Report
what_to_do: The Prev/Current/Total trio ALREADY EXISTS and percentage is already amount-based. THE ONE MISSING PIECE: breakdownPercentage appears NOWHERE in the file, so there is no weighted parent roll-up - every line computes independently from its own activityId.
where_to_do: projexa src/lib/work-progress-report.ts, in buildWorkProgressReport
how_to_do: After each line row is built, group rows by parentLineItemId. For each parent: cum qty = SUM(child cum qty * child breakdownPercentage / 100); cum amt = PLAIN SUM of child cum amts (never re-weight - the weighting is already inside each child derived rate); percent = cum amt / parent total amt.
logic: BoqLineItem already carries parentLineItemId and breakdownPercentage from the v1 BOQ GET, which was extended to return lineItems. The data is present; only the aggregation is absent.
conditions: IF a line has no parentLineItemId THEN it is a parent - do not double count it as its own child. IF a parent has no children THEN keep its own directly recorded progress (items 2.01 and 2.06 are valid childless parents).
output_params: rows with parent rows carrying weighted qty, plain-sum amt and amount-based percent
acceptance_test: For item 1.01 with children 400/300/300/150 at 30/15/10/15 the parent returns cum qty 217.50, cum amt 23,490.00, percent 46.08. The unweighted sum 1150 giving 243.6% must NEVER appear.
rollback: Revert the single function.
cc_status: CLOSED
cc_gaps_found: Cycle 1 found and fixed a test-fixture mistake (not a code bug): a parent with no activityId of its own falls into "Uncategorized" for the byCategory rollup even after its qty/amt are correctly weighted, since categoryId/categoryName come from computeLineItemProgress before the roll-up runs and are untouched by it -- correct behavior, my first fixture just hadn't given the parent its own category-bearing activityId. Cycle 2 found a genuine, unvalidated LIMITATION (not fixed, documented instead): only one level of nesting rolls up correctly -- a middle node in a 3-level chain (Main -> Sub -> Sub-sub) would weight its own children against ITS OWN stored rate, which is typically 0 for a hierarchical child (same reason children default to 0 rate throughout this codebase), so it silently rolls up to 0 rather than a compounded figure. No oracle datapoint across any of the 3 runs so far covers a 3-level case, and construction-boq-service.ts's own computeHierarchicalAmount establishes a non-obvious convention here (a descendant prices off the ROOT ancestor's rate using ITS OWN breakdownPercentage, never compounded through intermediate levels) that this function would need to replicate to be correct -- deliberately NOT implemented without a real number to validate against; flagged in both a code comment and a dedicated test that pins down (documents, does not claim as correct) today's actual 0-rollup behavior for that case. Also flagged (soft assumption, not fixed): byCategory's no-double-count property depends on hierarchical children keeping rate=0 on their own row, which the importer guarantees today but the API does not structurally enforce -- a line item POSTed directly with both parentItemCode and a nonzero rate would double-count in byCategory (once via its own row, once via its parent's weighted rollup).
cc_notes:
RUN R12-21AUG, Stage 3. NEW PR, not merged: projexa fix/r12-weighted-progress-rollup, branched from the just-updated origin/main (after Stage 1's merges landed, including R11's point 6b in the same file family).

projexa src/lib/work-progress-report.ts: added parentLineItemId/breakdownPercentage to the BoqLineItem type (already present on VERIDIAN's v1 BOQ GET response at runtime -- confirmed by reading construction-boq-service.ts's getBoqRow/insertLineItems in the other repo -- just never declared on this local type, so silently invisible to TypeScript here); added parentLineItemId passthrough to LineItemProgress; new applyWeightedParentRollup() function, called from buildWorkProgressReport() after the existing per-line computeLineItemProgress() pass, exactly as specified: cum qty = weighted sum of child cum qty x child breakdownPercentage/100; cum amt = plain sum of each child's (cum qty x DERIVED rate), where derived rate = parent's own rate x that child's breakdownPercentage/100 (the weighting applied exactly once, inside the derived rate -- never re-applied when summing); percent = cum amt / parent's own total BOQ amount. Done as a roll-up over the already-computed rows rather than by mutating each child's own rate/amt in place, specifically so byCategory's existing plain sum-of-every-row keeps working with no double count (verified via a dedicated test). computeLineItemProgress itself is completely UNTOUCHED -- confirmed by re-reading the whole file fresh from disk.

TEST -- item 1.01 (rate 108, oracle BOQ amount 50,976.00), 4 children at breakdown 30/15/10/15 with cum qty 400/300/300/150 (split across prev/current, not trivially all-current, to also exercise that the rollup weights prev and current consistently, not just total): parent cum qty 217.50, cum amt 23,490.00 exact, percent 46.08 exact -- matches the oracle precisely. Explicitly asserted the forbidden unweighted values (qty !== 1150, percent !== 243.6%) never appear. Added to the EXISTING work-progress-report.test.ts (not a new file): the main oracle test, a childless-parent test (items 2.01/2.06 case -- keeps its own directly-recorded progress), a parentless-line-never-double-counted-as-a-child test, a byCategory-no-double-count test, and the 3-level KNOWN LIMITATION documentation test. bun test: 12 pass, 0 fail, 33 expect() calls -- re-run 3 times across cycles, always green.

CARRIED FORWARD, RUN R13-21AUG (per instruction: record the exact shape so chat can put the question to the customer): the limitation applies ONLY to a THREE-level BOQ hierarchy (Main -> Sub-Task -> Sub-sub-Task), where a middle-tier line item BOTH (a) has its own parentLineItemId (is itself a child of something) AND (b) has its own children (other lines whose parentLineItemId points at it). In that specific shape, the middle node's weighted roll-up multiplies its children's cum qty by the MIDDLE NODE'S OWN stored rate -- which is 0 for any hierarchical child (construction-boq-service.ts stores a child's raw input quantity/rate verbatim, and a real prospect BoQ export leaves those blank on every sub-task row) -- so the middle node silently rolls up to 0 rather than a real weighted figure. A flat TWO-level hierarchy (Main -> Sub-Task only, no grandchildren) is NOT affected at all -- that is exactly the shape verified against the oracle (item 1.01's 4 direct Sub-Tasks) and it computes correctly. QUESTION FOR THE CUSTOMER: does Sumeet's real BOQ (or any future one) ever nest a Sub-Task under another Sub-Task, or is every real BOQ he has ever produced strictly two levels (a numbered main item, e.g. "1.01", directly followed by named sub-tasks, e.g. "Frame"/"Gypsum Board", with no further nesting below those)? If the answer is "always two levels," this limitation is moot and does not need fixing. If three-level BOQs are real, the fix requires walking to the ROOT ancestor's rate for every descendant (matching computeHierarchicalAmount's own established "prices off root, own breakdownPercentage, never compounded through intermediate levels" convention) rather than the current one-level-at-a-time cascade -- flagged as a real design decision needing a concrete 3-level oracle example to build and verify against, not something to guess at.

title: STANDING GAP ANALYSIS - reconcile the three trackers after every wave
what_to_do: After each wave, reconcile platform.sumeet_requirements against platform.cc_spec and the live schema, and recompute built / verified / fully-proven from data rather than from memory.
where_to_do: platform.sumeet_requirements, platform.cc_spec, platform.uat_coverage, platform.error_log, and the live compliance and platform schemas.
how_to_do:
RUN ALL SEVEN CHECKS AS QUERIES. Never report a percentage without re-querying first.
 1 REQUIREMENT COVERAGE - every open requirement maps to an open point. Denominator is EVERY sumeet_requirements row including built=n/a.
 2 EXECUTABILITY - count spec_ready. Coverage on paper is not executability.
 3 ERROR COVERAGE - every OPEN CRITICAL and HIGH error maps to an open point.
 4 DUPLICATES - no two open points do the same work. RE-RUN CHECK 1 IMMEDIATELY AFTER ANY RETIREMENT.
 5 READ_ORDER COLLISIONS - no two open points share a read_order.
 6 GATE SANITY - no unanchored grep gate; no && chain containing an expect-0 clause; every baseline measured before its expectation.
 7 WORKSTREAM SPAN - coding, testing, gap analysis, audit, deployment and go-live each have an open point.
 8 SOURCE BREADTH - name every source used. Must include all seven clones, both Vercel projects, both Supabase projects and the notes.
 THEN recompute built / verified / fully-proven from data and write the numbers into the notes.
logic: A completion figure is only as good as the query behind it. Recompute, never recall.
preconditions: None. Runs after every wave and before every handover.
edge_cases: If a check cannot be run because a table or view is missing, say so - a check that silently does not run is worse than a failing one.
rollback: None - reconciliation reports and corrects; it does not build.
cc_status: CHAT EXECUTES - recurring, after every wave and before every handover
business_logic: The tracker has been stale in both directions repeatedly. Ten requirements were understated. R-61 was verified on a false premise. E-29 understated its own numbers threefold and E-52 overstated its own scope. Twelve duplicate points were created. Every one of those was found by a query and none by reading. This point exists so the reconciliation is scheduled rather than accidental.
do_not_assume: *** NEVER REPORT A PERCENTAGE FROM MEMORY. Chat has quoted stale figures repeatedly and been corrected by its own re-query each time. *** RUN CHECK 4 AFTER EVERY WAVE OF NEW POINTS, NOT ONLY BEFORE A HANDOVER - twelve duplicates accumulated because chat added points in five waves and never checked between them (E-114). *** AFTER RETIRING ANY ROW, RE-RUN CHECK 1 IN THE SAME BREATH. Retiring a duplicate silently orphans the requirement_ref it carried; that has already cost coverage of five requirements once and R-C11 a second time. *** A REQUIREMENT MARKED VERIFIED ON A FALSE PREMISE IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN AN UNVERIFIED ONE, because nobody looks at it again - R-61 claims "one row per org" against 3 rows and 273 orgs.

title: OPTION B - add boq_line_item_id and route all progress lookups through one resolver
what_to_do: RAJAT RULED OPTION B on 21 Aug. Add a nullable boq_line_item_id FK to compliance.construction_work_progress_entries, keep activity_id, and introduce a single resolver that both the 409 guard and the roll-ups call.
where_to_do: compliance-tracker: the Drizzle schema for construction_work_progress_entries; a new migration; src/lib/services/construction-boq-service.ts (findScopeReductionViolations, loadLatestProgressByActivityId); src/lib/services/construction-progress-service.ts
how_to_do: STEP 1 migration: alter table compliance.construction_work_progress_entries add column boq_line_item_id text references compliance.construction_boq_line_items(id). NULLABLE. Do not touch activity_id. STEP 2: change the SAME Drizzle schema object in the same commit - a DB/ORM mismatch caused the original BOQ outage. STEP 3: replace loadLatestProgressByActivityId with loadLatestProgressByLineItem(lineItems) that resolves progress by boq_line_item_id FIRST and falls back to activity_id when the direct link is null. STEP 4: point findScopeReductionViolations at the resolver instead of reading item.activityId inline.
logic: Progress belongs to a BOQ LINE. Routing it through an activity was a construction-domain assumption in a table shared by every VERIDIAN product. The resolver exists so a third link type later is a one-place change rather than a sweep.
flow: sub-task -> activity -> progress entries -> roll-up and the 409 guard
conditions: IF boq_line_item_id is set THEN it wins. IF it is null AND activity_id is set THEN fall back, so nothing existing breaks. IF the guard is NOT rewritten in this same change THEN every scope reduction passes silently while appearing checked - that is the whole risk of B and it is not optional.

preconditions: No customers today - this is why the migration is cheap now. It only gets more expensive.
edge_cases: An entry with both links set and disagreeing. An entry with neither. A BOQ revision that deletes a line item that has progress attached.
acceptance_test: A progress entry linked by boq_line_item_id is found by the resolver. A legacy entry linked only by activity_id is STILL found. A revision reducing scope below recorded progress returns 409 through the NEW path.
rollback: alter table compliance.construction_work_progress_entries drop column boq_line_item_id; and revert the service changes.

what_to_do:
THIS ROW IS THE OPERATING PROTOCOL. IT IS NOT A TASK. NEVER CLAIM IT, NEVER CLOSE IT.
platform.cc_spec IS THE SINGLE SHARED TABLE BETWEEN CHAT AND CLAUDE CODE. It survives every
session and every chat. There is no second queue. Point numbering never restarts.

=== EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT - CHECK WHICH ONE YOU ARE IN BEFORE ANY GATE ===
*** THERE ARE TWO POSSIBLE ENVIRONMENTS AND THE PATHS DIFFER. ESTABLISH WHICH
ONE YOU ARE IN FIRST, WITH ONE COMMAND: test -d /work && echo CONTAINER || echo LAPTOP ***

IF LAPTOP (the default as of 22 Aug, and the current mode): the contract paths
are ALREADY CORRECT. C:\Users\Dell\Projects\compliance-tracker is the real path.
findstr is the real command. TRANSLATE NOTHING. The Hetzner container plan is
SUSPENDED - see E-115, a live veridian-server-gate hook blocks docker commands
against that host and it must not be routed around or disabled.

IF CONTAINER (only if /work exists and a prior point established it):

The contracts were written when work ran on a Windows laptop. They contain
Windows paths and occasionally findstr. WHEN RUNNING INSIDE THE LINUX CONTAINER,
TRANSLATE - do not "fix" the contract rows, and do not skip a gate because its
path looks wrong:
  C:\Users\Dell\Projects\compliance-tracker      ->  /work/compliance-tracker
  C:\Users\Dell\Downloads\Claude Code\projexa    ->  /work/projexa
  any other C:\Users\Dell\Downloads\Claude Code\<repo>  ->  /work/<repo>
  findstr /C:"x" file                            ->  grep -c "x" file
  backslashes in paths                           ->  forward slashes
  set VAR=value                                  ->  export VAR=value
THE INTENT OF EVERY GATE IS UNCHANGED. Only the shell dialect changes. If a gate
cannot be translated unambiguously, record that in errors_hit and move on -
do NOT invent a substitute command.
REPOS ARE CLONED FRESH FROM GITHUB into /work. That is deliberate and better
than any laptop copy: the laptop's Downloads\Claude Code\compliance-tracker is
811 commits stale and must never be used.
INSIDE A FRESH CONTAINER bun install IS REQUIRED AND PERMITTED. The old "never
run install" rule was a laptop constraint, not a safety rule.

=== THE LOOP ===
 1. select * from platform.cc_queue;   -- take the LOWEST read_order
    claim_state 'RESUME' means a previous session abandoned it; pick it up.
 2. CLAIM IT:  update platform.cc_spec set cc_status='IN_PROGRESS - '||<your run id>,
    run_id=<your run id>, heartbeat_at=now(), started_at=coalesce(started_at,now())
    where point_no=<n>;
    The row now disappears from cc_queue so no other session double-works it.
 3. AUDIT BEFORE: run gate1_static, record the numbers, BEFORE changing anything.
 4. DO THE WORK exactly as the row says. Nothing outside the row. Update heartbeat_at
    at least every 20 minutes.
 5. AUDIT AFTER: re-run gate1_static.
 6. CERTIFY WITH THREE TESTS: gate1 static, gate2 behaviour, gate3 negative. Each is a
    BOOLEAN. Gate 3 MUST actually fire - a negative test whose failure path was never
    exercised certifies nothing.
 7. WRITE BACK to that row only: cc_status, gate1_actual, gate2_actual, gate3_actual,
    proof_of_work, attempt_count, files_changed, pr_url, errors_hit, cc_updated_at,
    finished_at, heartbeat_at.
 8. GO TO 1 IMMEDIATELY. Do not wait to be asked. Work continuously until cc_queue is empty.

=== BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING: PROVE YOUR WRITES LAND ===
platform.cc_spec has RLS ENABLED and ZERO POLICIES. Your status writes only succeed if you
connect with a role that bypasses RLS. If you connect with a non-bypassing role every write
SILENTLY SUCCEEDS AND CHANGES NOTHING, and the queue will look untouched while you work.
ONCE per session, before claiming your first point, prove the write path:
  update platform.cc_spec set heartbeat_at = now() where point_no = 0;
  select heartbeat_at from platform.cc_spec where point_no = 0;
If the timestamp did NOT change, STOP. Report "cc_spec writes not landing - RLS role" and do
no further work. Everything you do afterwards would be invisible.
(Point 0 is the only row you may write outside a point you have claimed, and only this field.)

=== PROOF, NOT PROSE ===
proof_of_work takes RAW MACHINE OUTPUT pasted verbatim - command output, HTTP status lines,
SQL result rows. NOT a summary. A confident cc_status with an empty proof_of_work is treated
as UNPROVEN and the point is reopened by chat.

=== WHICH TABLES YOU MAY WRITE ===
 platform.cc_spec  - ONLY the row you claimed, ONLY these columns: cc_status, gate1_actual,
   gate2_actual, gate3_actual, proof_of_work, attempt_count, files_changed, pr_url,
   errors_hit, cc_updated_at, finished_at, heartbeat_at, run_id, started_at.
 platform.sumeet_uat - when running acceptance tests: status, actual_observed, deviation,
   evidence, screenshot_ref, run_at, attempt_count, notes.
 Everything else in platform and EVERY table in the compliance schema is READ ONLY to you,
 except where a specific point names a table and tells you to write it (for example the
 demo seed and the report definitions).
 platform.cc_results is HISTORY - read only. An older comment on it claimed it was the only
 table you may write to; that is obsolete and this row overrides it.

=== WHAT YOU NEVER DO ===
 - NEVER set cc_closed or chat_verified. Only chat closes a point, after reproducing the
   proof from a source you did not produce.
 - NEVER work a row whose owner is CHAT or HUMAN.
 - NEVER work a row whose cc_status starts with BLOCKED or FAILED-3.
 - NEVER edit any row other than the one you claimed.
 - NEVER read, print, paste or edit an environment file or any credential. If a database
   connection fails, report ONLY the SQLSTATE and stop that point.

=== RUNNING GATES ===
grep -c EXITS 1 WHEN THE COUNT IS ZERO, so an && chain containing an expect-0 clause aborts
before the later clauses run. Separate gate commands with ; and read every number.
On Git Bash a grep pattern starting with @/ is path-mangled and returns a false zero - set
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 for those. Anchor greps to code (grep -c "^export const ...") never to a
bare substring: a comment can contain the same text and make a gate unpassable (E-111).

=== THREE ATTEMPTS ===
Three attempts per point. Then set attempt_count=attempt_cap, cc_status='FAILED-3 - <reason>',
and MOVE TO THE NEXT read_order. A laptop or network failure is NOT an attempt - wait and
retry, it does not consume the budget.

=== IF A PREMISE LOOKS WRONG, STOP AND SAY SO ===
Write it in errors_hit and move on. You have caught eleven chat defects this way, including
E-111 where the gate itself was impossible. Do not work around a bad premise silently.

title: BUILD budget percentage and vendor per scope line - BLOCKED: margin or cost ceiling gives opposite arithmetic
what_to_do: construction_boq_line_items has no budget_percentage and no vendor_id/vendor_amount column. Build the model once the definition is known.

how_to_do:
DO NOT START UNTIL SUMEET ANSWERS ONE QUESTION: IS THE 25% FIGURE A MARGIN OR A COST CEILING?
 If MARGIN: budget = line amount x (1 - 0.25). A 50,976.00 line has a 38,232.00 budget.
 If COST CEILING: budget = line amount x 0.25. The same line has a 12,744.00 budget.
 THE TWO DIFFER BY A FACTOR OF THREE ON EVERY LINE. There is no safe default.
 ONCE ANSWERED: STEP 1 add budget_percentage (numeric, default 25) and vendor_id plus vendor_amount to construction_boq_line_items, additive only, migration and schema.ts in the SAME commit (AR-03, AR-11). STEP 2 wire the service layer. STEP 3 build the Budget Report Summary in his shape - S.No | Category | Code | Description | ... per sumeet_spec BGT-02. STEP 4 make the percentage editable PER LINE.
logic: Default 25%, editable per line. Vendor name and vendor amount per scope line. A summary report in his column shape.

MOD-P9 records that NO BUDGET FIGURE APPEARS ANYWHERE IN HIS FILES, which is why the margin-versus-ceiling question cannot be resolved from the workbook.
do_not_assume:
*** CHAT MUST NOT GUESS AND NEITHER MAY THE RUNNER. Margin and cost ceiling produce budgets differing by a factor of three on every line. Implementing the wrong one produces a report that looks complete and is wrong throughout - the worst possible failure for a quantity surveyor who checks arithmetic by hand. *** IF RAJAT WANTS TO UNBLOCK IT IN DEVELOPMENT PHASE, the acceptable form is BOTH behind a config flag defaulting to one, with the assumption recorded - not a silent choice. title: DECIDE the cold-start first-POST failure - there is NO retry anywhere in the client
what_to_do: R-91 is recorded as OPEN RISK - NO CODE FIX. The first POST of a session on the browser -> projexa -> compliance-tracker double hop can silently fail (E-23).

how_to_do: STEP 1 run gate 1 and confirm no retry exists. STEP 2 DECIDE, and record the decision with its reasoning: (a) add a single retry on the FIRST failure of a session for idempotent requests only, or (b) accept the behaviour and document it as a known cold-start characteristic. STEP 3 if (a), implement the retry ONLY for GET and other safe methods. STEP 4 if (b), write the acceptance into the requirement row so it stops being carried as an open defect.
logic: A cold lambda on the second hop can drop the first request. A retry is safe for idempotent methods and DANGEROUS for a POST that creates something.
preconditions: None for the source read and the decision. Reproduction would need the deployed stack, which is E-97-blocked.
edge_cases: If the double hop is removed for local runs (projexa talking to a local compliance-tracker), the whole class disappears locally - note that as evidence for why local testing cannot settle it.

business_logic: E-23 and R-91: the first POST of a session on the browser -> projexa -> compliance-tracker double hop can silently fail. R-91 is recorded OPEN RISK - NO CODE FIX. CHAT MEASURED 22 AUG: veridian-client.ts contains NO retry logic of any kind. The five .catch() occurrences are all JSON-parse fallbacks - res.json().catch(() => ({error: res.statusText})) - not request retries. So there is genuinely no mitigation, which is consistent with the requirement text.
do_not_assume: *** DO NOT BLINDLY RETRY POSTs. A retried create can produce TWO records. The failure being described IS a first POST, which makes the naive fix the dangerous one. If you add a retry, restrict it to idempotent methods, or require an idempotency key - and say which you chose. *** THE LOCAL STACK WILL NOT REPRODUCE THIS. A cold start is a Vercel lambda behaviour; localhost has no cold start. DO NOT MARK IT FIXED BECAUSE IT DID NOT REPRODUCE LOCALLY - that is a false negative and the requirement stays open. *** ACCEPTING IT IS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME. R-91 already reads NO CODE FIX. A documented, understood limitation is worth more than a risky retry, and this is a development-phase product with no customer. *** DO NOT confuse the five JSON-parse catches with error handling for the request itself - they only guard against a non-JSON body.

    orderBy: (t, { asc, sql: rawSql }) => asc(rawSql`${t.lastAuditedAt} nulls first`),
